parsed.rationale: Four separate `extension` declarations on `String` are spread across three distinct packages (`Playlist`, `AnalyticsMacros`, `Analytics`), creating name-collision risk and making it difficult to audit what capabilities are being added to `String` across the codebase. The dedicated file `String+HTMLDecoding.swift` in the `Playlist` package suggests at least one extension is already intentionally scoped, but the remaining three are embedded inside unrelated files (`FlowsheetEntryType.swift` line 106, `AnalyticsEventMacro.swift` line 154, `AnalyticsEvent.swift` line 39), which is a maintenance smell. Where cross-package sharing is not needed, each package should consolidate its `String` extensions into a single, clearly named `String+<Domain>.swift` file; where functionality is genuinely shared (e.g., HTML decoding used by both `Playlist` and `Analytics`), it should be extracted to a common lower-level package that all consumers already depend on. No context flags (`is_test`, `is_codegen`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`) are set on any member, so this is production code warranting action.
